about.metaDescription: About {site} — open-source desktop software for life sciences.

blocks.text: {site} hosts a collection of free, open-source desktop software developed for biological research

I believe in the collaborative scientific spirit. Good tools save time for scientists. By making such tools open and accessible instead of locking them behind commerical licenses, we can benefit from each other's work and accelerate research together.

items.text: Each gets its own site with an overview, requirements, installation steps and a download that always points at the current release.

items.strong: A short list of {total} other tools.
items.text: Software from other groups that we use ourselves, pointing you to each project's own website and, where there is one, its source repository.

blocks.text: This is a short, opinionated list rather than an exhaustive index. A tool earns a place only if:

items: We use it ourselves in real work.
It is free to obtain, without registration or a licence request.
It has a graphical interface that is easy to use — desktop or browser.
It runs locally on your computer without internet dependencies

blocks.text: Most of these are open source, which is what we prefer and what we build. A few are free to use without being open source — UCSF ChimeraX is free for academic use, Obsidian is free for personal use, and Visual Studio Code's source is MIT while Microsoft's own builds carry their licence. We list those anyway because they earn their place, and the licence badge on each entry says exactly what you are getting rather than glossing over it.

We are not affiliated with any of these projects, and listing is not endorsement by them of us. We deliberately do not host or link to installers: each entry sends you to the project's own site, so you always download from the maintainers themselves and see their current instructions. Names and trademarks belong to their respective owners.
The whole site is a public repository. If a link has rotted, a description is wrong, or a tool deserves a place in the directory, open an issue or send a pull request.
